model_interpretation.claim: Among the recorded valid SIMD candidates, runtime-peeled 16-byte alignment measured 0.079254 s, guarded SIMD without an alignment clause measured 0.079892 s, and 64-byte alignment measured 0.087704 s. This candidate tests an intermediate 32-byte boundary: each contiguous interior row checks the actual residues of input, velocity, and output pointers, scalar-peels to a common aligned start when possible, and otherwise uses unaligned guarded SIMD. It makes no ISA or allocation-alignment assumption, and the close 16-byte/unaligned results are not evidence of a stable gain.

model_interpretation.claim: Rebasing each contiguous x row at row_base + x0 and expressing the stencil with unit-stride line pointers may make the unfused scalar loop easier for the frozen compiler's automatic vectorizer to optimize, without an OpenMP SIMD directive or alignment assumption. items.subject: Single-sweep x-line kernel vectorization
items.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, isolate the unfused single-timestep kernel and contiguous-x line traversal. Compare the existing scalar formulation with compiler-vectorizable and, only if supported by the frozen build, explicit SIMD formulations; do not change compiler flags or assume an ISA extension. Account for the interior start offset despite aligned inputs. Keep threading and spatial/temporal blocking out of scope. Preserve numerical tolerance and boundaries; validate and measure the kernel under the official settings.
